 Govt bearing over ₹325/cylinder in LPG supply cost
 The under recovery is expected to rise further to roughly ₹370 per cylinder in December 2026 as the benchmark Saudi CP price is also rising in line with the demand season in winter
 By Rishi Ranjan Kala 
 Updated - November 16, 2026 at 07:59 PM. × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/govt-bearing-over-325cylinder-in-lpg-supply-cost/article71708557.ece Copy 
 For the week ended November 13, 2026, propane prices fell 2.1 per cent w-o-w to $604.6 per tonne, according to Equirus Research
 | Photo Credit:
 RAGHUNATHAN SR
 In a bid to make liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) more economical for the common man, the government is bearing ₹325.24 per cylinder, which is the cost of supplying the 14.2 kg domestic cylinder to the end consumer. 
 This is besides the expected under recovery of roughly ₹327 per cylinder for November 2026 that is being borne by the PSU Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) — Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL).
 The under recovery is expected to rise further to roughly ₹370 per cylinder in December 2026 as the benchmark Saudi CP price is also rising in line with the demand season in winter.
 The PSU OMCs are selling the 14.2 kg domestic LPG cylinder to the domestic consumer at ₹942 per cylinder and at ₹642 per cylinder to the PM Ujjawala Yojna (PMUY) beneficiaries against the market cost of ₹1,268.24 per cylinder.
 For the week ended November 13, 2026, propane prices fell 2.1 per cent w-o-w to $604.6 per tonne, according to Equirus Research.
 As of September 30, 2026, IOCL’s cumulative under recovery on LPG was ₹32,505.69 crore. BPCL and HPCL reported under recoveries of ₹17,334.40 crore and ₹18,048.82 crore, respectively.
 India primarily uses LPG for cooking and is used by roughly 32.67 crore households, which also includes around 10.57 crore PMUY beneficiaries (September 2026).
 The country’s cumulative domestic LPG sales declined by 13.5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) to 12.19 million tonnes (mt) during H1 FY27. The decline in consumption is primarily due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz (SoH), which accounts for around 90 per cent of India’s total imports.
 The closure of the SoH pushed the government to enhance production of the key cooking fuel. During H1 FY27, the world’s second largest consumer produced roughly 7.86 mt of LPG, a growth of 25.16 per cent on an annual basis. Average monthly LPG production also rose to 1.31 mt in H1 FY27 from 1.05 mt per month in H1 FY26.
 Kpler recently said that it expects India’s LPG demand is likely to decline by around 100,000 barrels per day (b/d) in 2026 as SoH closure impacted imports. Priti Mehta, Kpler’s Senior Oil Demand Modelling Analyst, anticipated that LPG demand will recover from its Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 lows during Q4, supported by the festival season and higher imports, but the recovery is expected to remain incomplete.
 However, demand is forecast to increase by only around 60,000 b/d in 2027, recovering slightly more than half of the 2026 decline. Part of the remaining loss is likely to be structural as the government promotes PNG connections, particularly among urban households connected to city gas distribution networks, she added .
